subject: Production access cutover: IP allowlists, SCIM scope, and service account delegation
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production access cutover: IP allowlists, SCIM scope, and service account delegation

Sam — thanks again for the productive call this morning. As promised, I’m sending a concise execution plan so your infra and security teams can validate before we schedule the cutover window. High-level asks below and attachments included.

Immediate asks (please confirm by EOD Tuesday):
- Finalize external IP ranges for our egress allowlist (attached CSV) — we need CIDR entries and the owner contact.
- Confirm the SCIM provisioning scope: users only, or groups+users? See scim-provisioning-scope.md attached; we recommend groups+users for role mappings.
- Approve the service-account mapping sheet so CS can provision minimal-priv SA with scoped keys (service-account-mapping.xlsx).

Planned cutover steps (tentative):
1) Dry run in staging (we’ll run a 30-min provisioning exercise)
2) Apply IP allowlist updates and SCIM scope in staging; validate provisioning flows
3) Nighttime production cutover with rollback window (30 mins)
4) Post-cutover smoke and audit logs handed to Acme security

I’ve looped Ben for the staging runbook and Monica to own the SCIM mapping review. Jordan will coordinate schedule with your SREs. If anything in the attachments is off, flag inline and we’ll iterate.

Thanks — Priyom
Priyom Das
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmecorp.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T10:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production access cutover: IP allowlists, SCIM scope, and service account delegation

Thanks, Priyom — this looks good. A couple quick notes from our side after internal sync: 
- IP ranges: we will provide the production egress CIDRs by EOD Tuesday; Lisa will own that and is CC'd.
- SCIM: security prefers groups+users but need confirmation that group push supports nested groups (our IDP uses nested groups for teams). Can you confirm?
- Service accounts: we require an audit trail for SA key ops and a short-lived key approach if possible. Please confirm the options.

We can target Friday 2026-10-15 for the staging dry run in the morning (09:00 PT). I’ll loop our SREs in a follow-up thread once the staging runbook is ready.

Sam
Sam Patel
Director of IT, AcmeCorp
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production access cutover: IP allowlists, SCIM scope, and service account delegation

Looping in our staging runbook and checklist (excerpt below). I’ll attach the full runbook to the Drive link once we finalize times.

Staging dry-run checklist (short):
- Provision test tenant and map a 5-user group via SCIM (verify group-to-role mapping)
- Apply IP allowlist entries from acmecorp-ip-allowlist.csv to staging FW rules
- Create SA with scoped permissions; exercise token rotation and record audit events
- Validate session token TTLs and rate limits

On nested groups: our SCIM connector supports nested groups for mappings but we need the exact group DN patterns. Monica — can you work with Lisa to confirm group nesting rules and produce 2 sample group DNs?

Ben
Ben Carter
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acmecorp.com>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmecorp.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: SCIM mapping questions + sample DNs

On Mon, Oct 12, 2026 at 08:03 Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com> wrote:
> Sam — quick follow-up on nested groups. Our connector can accept nested group DNs with a straightforward mapping template. Can you send 2 example group DNs from your IdP so we can validate?

Lisa — attaching a short doc (scim-provisioning-scope.md) and a template for group DNs. If you can paste two real DNs, we’ll run them in staging tomorrow. Also including the service-account-mapping.xlsx with required columns: SA name, minimum scopes, owner email, suggested rotation TTL.

Attachments referenced: scim-provisioning-scope.md (doc), service-account-mapping.xlsx (spreadsheet)

— Monica
Monica Patel
Security Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acmecorp.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-13T15:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production access cutover: IP allowlists, SCIM scope, and service account delegation

Monica — pasted two sample DNs below and attached our final IP list (acmecorp-ip-allowlist.csv). We reviewed with our security team; nested groups are allowed but lookups are limited to two levels deep.

Sample group DNs:
- CN=eng-team,OU=Teams,OU=Groups,DC=acme,DC=com
- CN=eng-leads,OU=Managers,OU=Groups,OU=Regions,DC=acme,DC=com

Service account requirements:
- Audit trail: we can accept centrally logged key operations if Redwood publishes key-creation and rotation events to our SIEM (we can provide a webhook or accept CloudWatch logs).
- Short-lived keys: we prefer a 1-hour TTL for tokens; please confirm whether Redwood supports ephemeral tokens for SA use.

We’re confirmed for a staging dry run on 2026-10-15 at 09:00 PT. Please send the Drive runbook and an invite to our SRE group.

Thanks — Lisa
Lisa Chen
Senior Security Engineer, AcmeCorp
Attachments: acmecorp-ip-allowlist.csv
